title: Chapter 4 — Matriculation
description: The oath, the gown that doesn't fit, the society you join, and the one lecturer who reads your notes and actually likes them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Matriculation. Two thousand freshers in hired gowns, swearing to uphold the honour of Royal Crest University. Half of them are filming it. The other half are filming the first half.

beats.speaker: vc
beats.text: You are the future of this nation. Behave like it. Especially at the back gate. (Several people laugh. The VC does not.)

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: (two rows behind, whispering) Jambite. After this, back gate. Your first "dues" are due.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: (two rows behind, whispering) Security lost your report. Funny how files go missing. We haven't lost your face.

beats.objective: Walk the Quad: the societies have stalls out for freshers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Debate Society. Chapel Choir. Rotaract. Entrepreneurs' Club (three boys selling the same crypto). Each stall wants you, your time and ₦2,000.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Where will you spend your evenings?

options.text: Debate Society. You've argued with danfo drivers since you were six.
Chapel Choir. Quiet, free food on Sundays, nobody asks your father's job.
Nothing. Evenings are for reading and frying.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: (at the Debate Society table, as secretary, raising one eyebrow) You. The boy who reads prices. Prove you can talk as well as you read.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Thursday. ECO 101. A thin man with chalk on his trousers, Dr. Adébáyọ̀, gives back the first assignment by name.

beats.speaker: drBayo
beats.text: Mr. Somtochukwu. "Price discovery at a bus-stop pap stall". (He holds it up.) This is the only essay in the pile written by someone who has sold something. Stay after class.

beats.speaker: drBayo
beats.text: Royal Crest will try to teach you that economics happens in Abuja. It happens at bus stops. Never forget the bus stop.

beats.speaker: drBayo
beats.text: I run a reading group on Fridays. No handouts. No fees. Lots of arguing.

options.text: "Fridays are for my business, sir. Akara doesn't sell itself."

beats.title: Matriculation
beats.summary: You swore an oath in a borrowed gown, chose your evenings, and found the one lecturer who believes in bus stops.
